interest: Documents SCAP's 'Reverse Course' curbing public unions, U.S.-British policy friction, and Katayama Cabinet economic firefighting with Wada and Tsuru.
overview: Decimal file 894.5041 covers labor conditions, industrial wages, price stabilization, and the contentious evolution of public service labor legislation in occupied Japan between January 1947 and August 1949. Early documentation comprises transmittals of GHQ SCAP statistical reports on money wages compiled by the Japanese Cabinet Bureau of Statistics, alongside State Department economic analyses addressing protectionist fears that suppressed Japanese wages and unfair pre-war export practices would disrupt international trade. As post-war inflation mounted, the file focuses on the Katayama government's struggle to defend the 1,800-yen wage-price base and, most prominently, the high-stakes drafting and enactment of the revised National Public Service Law in late 1948. These records document fierce debates between SCAP Civil Service Chief Blaine Hoover, State Department officials, and the British Commonwealth over SCAP's sweeping ban on strikes and collective bargaining for all government and public corporation workers. The file concludes with an August 1949 diplomatic dispute regarding the British Commonwealth Occupation Force's delayed financial compliance with SCAP orders mandating occupation payment for Japanese domestic servants.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of GHQ SCAP Special Report No. 19 reporting average money wages across Japanese industries for August 1946.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Rolland H. Bushner)
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmits SCAP Special Report No. 19 (November 1946): average money wages in Japanese manufacturing, mining, transportation, and communications for August 1946, per the Cabinet Bureau of Statistics.
subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting SCAP Special Report No. 19 on average wages (August 1946)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of GHQ SCAP Special Report No. 21 reporting average money wages across Japanese industries for September 1946.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Rolland H. Bushner)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 824 transmits SCAP Special Report No. 21 (November 1946): average monthly wages in Japanese manufacturing, mining, transportation, and communications for September 1946, from the Cabinet Bureau of Statistics.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 824 transmitting SCAP Special Report No. 21 on average wages (September 1946)

subfiles.about: Cover memorandum transmitting Philip B. Sullivan's study on Japanese post-war labor costs to assist in responding to public inquiries on import competition.
subfiles.from: Kenneth A. Holland (ILH, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Holland forwards Sullivan's analysis of postwar Japanese labor costs to Carter in Public Liaison, to help answer domestic criticism of Japanese imports; a fuller analysis is planned.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Holland to Carter regarding Japanese labor costs
subfiles.to: Margaret R. T. Carter (PL, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Detailed economic assessment concluding that post-war Japan will not undersell foreign competitors based on cheap exploited labor as in pre-war years.
subfiles.from: Philip B. Sullivan (ILH, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Sullivan argues postwar Japanese exports won't undercut on cheap labor: unionization under SWNCC 92 topped 5.5 million workers by May 1947, with aggressive bargaining and sliding wage scales, while ending subsidies, zaibatsu practices, and new social insurance and labor-standards laws will raise costs, easing fears of unfair competition.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Sullivan on labor standards and labor costs in post-war Japan
subfiles.to: Charles A. Bane (CP, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a memorandum of conversation with Hiroo Wada and Shigeto Tsuru of the Economic Stabilization Board.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (W. Henry Lawrence, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1409 transmits a memo of a November 1947 conference with Wada and Tsuru of the Economic Stabilization Board on civil service wages, the 1,800-yen wage-price ceiling, personnel cuts, the purge's effect on business, and food price controls.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1409 transmitting memorandum of conversation with Economic Stabilization Board officials
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Division of Northeast Asian Affairs)

subfiles.about: Discussion with Japanese economic planners regarding government wage increases, the 1,800-yen wage ceiling, management purges, food price controls, and the dismissal of Rikizo Hirano.
subfiles.from: W. Henry Lawrence, Jr. (Second Secretary, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser)
subfiles.summary: Lawrence records Wada and Tsuru discussing raising public salaries while holding the 1,800-yen wage-price ceiling, shifting surplus staff to tax collection, the disruption from purging business executives, continued price controls on fish and vegetables, and Hirano's dismissal restoring Cabinet unity.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Hiroo Wada and Shigeto Tsuru of the Economic Stabilization Board
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Discussion between SCAP Civil Service Chief Blaine Hoover, British Embassy Counselor Graves, and State Department officials on the revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.summary: Hoover of SCAP's Civil Service Division argues for revising the National Public Service Law to end government unions' strike and bargaining rights, noting militant unions (40% of organized labor) had intimidated the Cabinet and Diet, and details new Personnel Authority compensation protections.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Blaine Hoover on the Japanese National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Arguments against issuing an interim directive overriding General MacArthur's restrictions on collective bargaining for Japanese civil servants.
subfiles.from: W. Walton Butterworth (Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs / NA)
subfiles.summary: W. Walton Butterworth strongly opposes a proposal by Edwin M. Martin and Robert W. Barnett urging an interim directive to compel SCAP to grant trade union and collective bargaining rights to Japanese government employees. Butterworth maintains that Blaine Hoover's National Personnel Authority framework adequately safeguards civil servants' welfare through mandatory cost-of-living reviews and independent grievance appeals, rendering American-style collective bargaining unnecessary. He warns that overriding General MacArthur would publicly weaken occupation authority, provoke political backlash in Congress, alienate Far Eastern Commission partners such as France and the Netherlands that back SCAP's interpretation, and risk political turmoil following the collapse of the Ashida Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Butterworth to Saltzman on revision of the Japanese National Public Service Law
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)

subfiles.about: Informal handwritten notes and departmental routing slip recording British Counselor Graves's representations regarding strike prohibitions in permanent Japanese legislation.
subfiles.from: P. F. Claxton / Charles E. Saltzman (O, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: These handwritten notes, accompanied by an Assistant Secretary routing slip dated November 29, 1948, document a discussion between Charles E. Saltzman (CES) and British Counselor H. A. Graves regarding British objections to pending Japanese labor legislation. The rough notes capture debates over whether SCAP should prohibit strikes administratively during the occupation rather than having the Japanese Diet enact permanent statutory prohibitions against government enterprise workers withholding their labor. They also reference communications with UK political representative Alvary Gascoigne and General MacArthur in Tokyo, serving as the contemporaneous basis for the formal memorandum of conversation drafted by P. F. Claxton.
subfiles.title: Routing slip and handwritten notes of conversation with Graves on Japanese labor legislation
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman / Department of State files

subfiles.about: Discussion of British objections to permanent statutory prohibitions against strikes and collective bargaining agreements in Japanese public corporations and civil service.
subfiles.from: P. F. Claxton (O, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Graves tells Saltzman and Allison that Britain accepts SCAP's wartime strike bans but opposes making permanent statutory bans on government-worker strikes and collective agreements part of Japanese law, asking the U.S. to relay British views to MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation between Graves and Saltzman on UK views on proposed Japanese National Public Service Bill

subfiles.about: Formal British critique of the National Public Service Bill and Public Corporations Bill, recommending independent arbitration and a 30-day cooling-off period.
subfiles.from: Government of the United Kingdom (British Embassy, Washington)
subfiles.summary: British memo on Japan's labor bills: Article 98 of the Public Service Bill should allow independent wage arbitration and not bar collective agreements; a permanent strike ban on public enterprise workers exceeds FEC policy, so London proposes a 30-day cooling-off period instead.
subfiles.title: United Kingdom memorandum on proposed amendments to Japanese labor legislation

subfiles.about: Review of British Commonwealth Occupation Force resistance to SCAP directives requiring payment for Japanese domestic servants and proposed diplomatic response.
subfiles.from: Niles W. Bond (NA, Department of State; drafted by Marshall Green)
subfiles.summary: Bond tells Allison that BCOF will pay for Japanese domestic servants per SCAP's 1948 directive but only from April 1949, not August 1948; officer Robertson resented SCAP's abrupt orders, and Bond recommends not pressing Australia for back pay.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Bond to Allison regarding BCOF payments for Japanese domestic servants
subfiles.to: John M. Allison (FE, Department of State)
